projects_no_hosts: No registered hosts — add one first.
projects_image_outdated: Base image update available — recreate this sandbox to get terminal improvements.
projects_agent_start_model_hint: Start a model to use this agent
credentials_intro: Log in once here to skip the per-sandbox login step. "Log out" removes the saved login from this device only — sandboxes that already received it stay authenticated.
credentials_github_help: Sent to package installs inside sandboxes to avoid GitHub's unauthenticated rate limit. Use a token with no scopes: install scripts inside the sandbox can read it. It is stored on this device and never shown again.
credentials_github_placeholder_replace: Paste a new token to replace it
podman_setup_description: This looks like your first run. Sandbox-mio needs to set up its container engine, which can take a few minutes.
podman_reboot_required: Windows needs to restart to finish installing WSL2. Restart your computer, then click Retry.
models_memory_warning: This model's RAM floor exceeds your free RAM; it may run slowly or fail to load.
settings_debugging_reset_machine_descrip: If Podman machine creation fails with a WSL import error, this clears the broken machine and its WSL registration so you can try creating it again.
settings_debugging_reset_machine_done: Reset complete. Try starting Podman again.
runtime_step_detect_device_explain: Detecting a Vulkan-capable GPU. llama.cpp uses the cross-vendor Vulkan API, so your Intel, AMD, or NVIDIA GPU works without vendor-specific drivers.
runtime_step_engine_ready_explain: Locating the bundled inference engine. The llama-server binary and its Vulkan libraries ship inside the app — nothing is installed on your system.
runtime_step_model_ready_explain: Preparing the model weights. The model is downloaded once and cached on disk; later starts reuse it.
runtime_step_launch_server_explain: Starting the local server. The model is loaded into memory and, where it fits, offloaded to the GPU for speed.
runtime_step_health_check_explain: Waiting for the server to report healthy, then exposing an OpenAI-compatible endpoint on your machine.
runtime_step_check_foundry_explain: Checking for Foundry Local, Microsoft's on-device AI runtime. Unlike llama.cpp it is a system component; if missing, the app can install it for you via winget.
runtime_step_register_eps_explain: Registering execution providers. Foundry picks the best accelerator on your PC — NPU, GPU, or CPU — through Intel OpenVINO and similar backends.
runtime_step_start_service_explain: Starting the Foundry inference service. It runs in the background and listens on a local port.
runtime_step_load_model_explain: Loading the model into the service so it is ready to answer requests.
runtime_step_resolve_id_explain: Reading back the exact served model name. Foundry serves a device-specific model ID that requests must use.
welcome_vm_technical_details: Sandboxes run inside a virtual machine. This sets it up on your computer.
welcome_podman_unresponsive_before: Podman started but never answered. Retrying may clear it; if it does not, the details are in
welcome_download_technical_details: Builds the base image every sandbox starts from. This takes a few minutes the first time.
welcome_wsl_reboot_message: Windows needs to restart to finish installing WSL2. Restart, then come back here.
projects_no_remote_target: This sandbox's provider has no remote deploy target.
netpolicy_drift: Changes pending — re-apply to recreate the sandbox with them.
netpolicy_mode_allowlist_hint: Only hosts allowed below are reachable; rules apply top to bottom, first match wins.
netpolicy_mode_open_hint: Every public host is reachable except what a deny rule below blocks.
secret_value_placeholder: value for the secret id above
netpolicy_echo_warning: {hosts} echoes requests back, so a bound secret's real value would reach the sandbox.
netpolicy_save_hint: Saving changes the workspace file only; the running sandbox keeps its policy until re-applied.
netpolicy_reapply_confirm: This recreates the sandbox VM around its workspace; tools installed outside the workspace are reinstalled from the lock file.
proxy_off_msb: Off. Turn it on below and re-apply the network settings.
proxy_off_podman: Off. Recreate this sandbox with inspection enabled to turn it on.
proxy_chained: Traffic is chained through this sandbox's mitmproxy VM.
proxy_stopped: The proxy sidecar is stopped. The sandbox's outbound requests fail until it restarts.
proxy_unmonitored: Traffic that ignores the proxy (raw sockets, git-over-SSH) is not inspected.
traffic_unhealthy: Proxy unreachable — requests fail closed until it answers again.
traffic_scope_msb: Shows TCP and HTTPS traffic only; DNS and UDP never reach the viewer.
traffic_secret_badge_title: A secret-injection rule matched this request
traffic_stopped: Proxy stopped — showing previously captured traffic.
welcome_intro_isolated: Sandbox mio gives every project its own isolated container, with its own runtime, terminal and AI coding agents.
welcome_intro_walkthrough: Let's walk through it together. There is a short setup first — two steps, and then you can create your first sandbox.
home_all_set_body: Everything is ready. Create your first sandbox to start working in it.
home_all_set_cta: Get started with your first sandbox
create_proxy_msb_hint: Runs a second VM (about 115 MiB) that sees every request, including substituted secret values.
create_egress_allowlist_hint: Only package registries, GitHub and the agents' APIs are reachable; edit the list after creating.
machine_step_wsl_install_explain: Podman sandboxes run inside a WSL2 virtual machine.
machine_step_machine_init_explain: Downloads the machine image on first run.
machine_step_socket_activate_explain: Starts the API the app talks to.
machine_step_msb_binary_explain: Checks the bundled msb CLI starts.
machine_step_msb_version_explain: Needs msb 0.7.12 or newer; the app ships its own copy, so reinstall sandbox-mio if this fails.
machine_step_hypervisor_platform_explain: Required for microsandbox's microVMs; enabling needs no restart.
machine_step_msb_doctor_explain: Confirms the host is ready to create sandboxes.
